meeting_header: Date: 2026-12-11; Start: 16:00 PST; Duration: 38m; Attendees: Lena Park (Redwood AE), Marcus Shaw (Redwood SE), Amira Singh (Pacifica VP Product), Jonas Meyer (Pacifica Head of ML), Sara Lee (Pacifica DevOps)
summary: Introductory console walkthrough focused on per-route usage insights and cost attribution. Demo of per-route dashboards, model-level cost breakdown, and Redwood Optimize recommendations (batching, caching, quantization). Security and deployment options discussed (Hosted vs Dedicated vs VPC). Agreed next steps: share pricing, route traces, and benchmark sheet; schedule pilot kickoff.
topics: Cost breakdown: model, route, and token-level
Optimize recommendations: batching, KV cache, quantization
Dedicated vs Hosted vs Private (VPC) tradeoffs
Security: SOC2, SSO/SAML, KMS, audit logs
transcript:
00:00 Lena Park: Hey everyone, uh welcome — I'm Lena from Redwood, thanks for joining. We've got about 40 minutes, we'll run through the console usage paths and per-route cost view, then leave time for Q&A.
00:12 Amira Singh: Thanks Lena, excited to see this. Our main ask is understanding per-route cost because we have a few high-volume triage flows.
00:24 Marcus Shaw: I'll drive the demo slides and then jump into the live console. Quick agenda: 1) high-level usage telemetry; 2) per-route dashboards; 3) Optimize suggestions for cost/latency tradeoffs; 4) security and deployment Qs.
00:39 Jonas Meyer: Great. Quick FYI — our traffic has a lot of very short chats and then some long inference for summaries. We care about both latency and cost.
00:50 Lena Park: Perfect, that mix is actually where the per-route telemetry shines.
01:02 Speaker 3: (muted)
01:10 Marcus Shaw: Alright switching to screen — here's the Console home. You can see top-level tokens per hour, cost burn rate, and a routes card. Note — route here maps to any API route or endpoint name, so you can map to your microservices if you want.
01:35 Amira Singh: Is that live data or a demo dataset?
01:40 Marcus Shaw: It's a masked demo dataset but configured to mimic a real traffic pattern. We'll share the exported CSV for the real product after.
01:52 Marcus Shaw: Jumping into routes, you can filter by model, region, and SLA tier. This route list shows requests, avg latency, p95, token distribution, and a cost column — that's per-route cost using our unit economics model.
02:12 Lena Park: One thing to call out — cost attribution includes model execution, GPU time, and tokenization overhead; it tries to map to what you'll actually be billed in hosted mode, and what you'd approximate for Dedicated.
02:31 Jonas Meyer: How precise is that attribution? If we run quantized models on Dedicated, will the console reflect that?
02:40 Marcus Shaw: Good question. The console has quantization profiles you can toggle — we model quantized throughput and per-token CPU/GPU mix. For Dedicated we ask you to select the capacity profile and we show an estimated per-token cost under that config. It's not perfect — think of it as a planning estimate.
02:58 Amira Singh: Okay. Can you show the route drilldown for our triage flow?
03:05 Marcus Shaw: Sure, opening route "triage-recommendation" — here you get a timeline of requests, a token histogram, model version breakdown, and a cost waterfall.
03:20 Marcus Shaw: The waterfall separates prompt tokens, generation tokens, and auxiliary costs like embeddings or rerank calls if you use them.
03:32 Amira Singh: Nice. What about caching? We have a lot of repeated prompts for triage templates.
03:38 Marcus Shaw: We have prefix and KV caching visible in the route view. You can see cache hit rate, hit latency delta, and how many tokens avoided. The Optimize panel will suggest enabling prefix caching or increasing TTLs when it detects patterns.
03:56 Lena Park: For example, in this demo the cache is reducing generated tokens by about 22% which directly drops cost.
04:05 Jonas Meyer: Is that automatic or do we need to change code?
04:11 Marcus Shaw: You need to integrate our SDK or use the API headers to mark cacheable inputs; Optimize gives code snippets and an estimated savings number.
04:25 Amira Singh: What about batching — we sometimes bundle micro-requests in our stream processing.
04:32 Marcus Shaw: The Optimize suggestions include batching profiles. There's a slider to trade latency for throughput; the console simulates expected p50/p95 under different batch sizes and shows token/sec improvements.
04:47 Speaker 1: (crosstalk)
04:51 Marcus Shaw: Going into the cost breakdown tab, you can pivot by model, by route, or by environment (prod/staging). You can also export CSVs for finance.
05:05 Amira Singh: Can we map this to our internal cost centers? e.g., by service owner?
05:11 Marcus Shaw: Yep — routes have metadata tags. You can attach cost center tags and then slice cost by tag. We'll show how to bulk-tag routes in the settings.
05:22 Sara Lee: On the security front — we need to validate that logs and tokens can be encrypted and access controlled.
05:29 Lena Park: Absolutely — Redwood Private supports VPC deployments, KMS/HSM for key control, and audit logs. Our hosted offering is SOC2 Type II and we have enterprise SSO/SAML.
05:45 Jonas Meyer: Any caveats about data residency? We have EU patients, so residency matters.
05:51 Lena Park: We support regional hosting options and Private deployments for strict residency. We'll include the compliance pack in the follow-up.
06:02 Amira Singh: Walk me through a hypothetical: we want to lower cost by 30% but keep p95 under 350ms.
06:09 Marcus Shaw: Good scenario — Optimize will run suggestions: 1) enable prefix cache for common prompts; 2) lower beam size / change sampling for certain routes; 3) route-level model pinning to lighter quantized variants; 4) use Dedicated for high-volume routes to reduce unit GPU costs. The console shows an estimated cost curve for each change and combined impact.
06:35 Marcus Shaw: I'm toggling a combined scenario — you can see cost drops to 28% and p95 goes from 420ms to 360ms in this demo. There's a preview of A/B rollout plan too so you can canary the change.
06:56 Amira Singh: That A/B rollout — does it handle automatic fallback if errors spike?
07:02 Marcus Shaw: Yes — you configure percentage rollouts and an automatic rollback policy based on error rate or latency SLOs. We also support fallback routing to a larger model or another region.
07:14 Lena Park: On the commercial side, Dedicated pricing is based on reserved GPU hours. We'll send a matrix but typically for very high-volume low-latency routes Dedicated is cheaper per token.
07:28 Sara Lee: Do you provide benchmarking in our environment? We want to run our own latency runs.
07:33 Marcus Shaw: We offer a pilot with benchmark tooling and will help run a per-route benchmark in your VPC or on a dedicated test cluster. We'll provide scripts that simulate your traffic pattern — that's part of the pilot proposal.
07:49 Jonas Meyer: About streaming and partial responses: we use streaming in one route. Does the console show the latency impact per token for streaming vs blocking?
07:58 Marcus Shaw: Yes, streaming metrics are included. You can see per-chunk latency, token throughput and also cost delta since streaming can keep connections open longer which impacts concurrency.
08:12 Amira Singh: Any gotchas for using quantized models with streaming?
08:18 Marcus Shaw: Minor — some kernels give slightly higher p50 but better cost; we surface that tradeoff in the profile. The runtime selects the best kernel based on seq length and hardware. Sometimes the transcription here may call it the "optimizer" but it's our Optimize product.
08:36 Speaker 2: (laughter)
08:40 Marcus Shaw: Switching to the rolls — I mean routes list, you can select multiple routes and run a bulk Optimize suggestion. It will produce a report with suggested batching, cache TTLs, and model assignments.
08:53 Amira Singh: Can we automate applying suggestions?
08:57 Marcus Shaw: There's an API endpoint and an infra playbook that can apply harmless config changes; for risky changes we push as suggestions only. We never automatically switch models without explicit approval.
09:11 Lena Park: On permissions, Console has RBAC — you can restrict who can run rollouts, who can tag routes, who can view cost.
09:21 Sara Lee: Good. We'll need SSO + SCIM so we can manage in Okta.
09:25 Lena Park: We support SAML/SCIM provisioning. We'll include the SSO integration guide.
09:33 Marcus Shaw: Now demoing the Optimize panel — it runs a quick evaluation across historical traffic and ranks suggestions by ROI. You can click into suggestion 3 which recommends increasing prefix TTL and model quantization for the triage route.
09:54 Marcus Shaw: Note the estimated avoided tokens and the confidence band. This is based off our cost models and your chosen deployment profile.
10:05 Amira Singh: How do you measure quality regressions? We can't accept lower accuracy without test coverage.
10:12 Marcus Shaw: We integrate with eval sets. You upload a small prompt-response test set and Optimize runs a quick regression check showing quality delta. It ties suggestions to an eval score so you can set thresholds.
10:28 Jonas Meyer: Will the regression check capture edge cases? We have safety checks in pipelines.
10:34 Marcus Shaw: It's a developer tool — it's only as good as your eval set. We recommend a few focused prompt sets for safety-critical routes.
10:43 Lena Park: Quick note on billing: you can get token-level invoices or aggregated. For finance teams we export CSVs broken down by tag and route.
10:55 Amira Singh: Great. We'd like an invoice that maps to our cost center tags.
11:00 Marcus Shaw: That's available.
11:05 Speaker 3: (background noise)
11:12 Marcus Shaw: Any other questions on the console UI?
11:16 Amira Singh: Onboarding timeline — if we do a pilot, how long to get meaningful results?
11:21 Lena Park: Typical pilot is 4–6 weeks: 1 week to instrument routes and export traces, 2 weeks to run benchmarks and pilot changes, 1–2 weeks to evaluate and iterate. We'll tailor.
11:34 Jonas Meyer: For the pilot, is Dedicated required?
11:37 Marcus Shaw: Not required. Many pilots run on hosted endpoints to validate behavior, then move to Dedicated if volume and economics justify it. If you need private residency we can run the pilot in your VPC.
11:51 Amira Singh: Can you show the CSV export quickly?
11:55 Marcus Shaw: Sure — exporting now. Here's the sample CSV: timestamp, route, model, tokens_in, tokens_out, cost_estimate, tag. You can feed that into your finance system.
12:11 Sara Lee: On logs retention — what's default?
12:14 Lena Park: Hosted defaults vary, but enterprise plans let you set retention windows; audit logs can be pushed to your SIEM or S3.
12:24 Amira Singh: This looks promising. Any known limits for concurrent streaming connections?
12:30 Marcus Shaw: Depends on plan and instance sizes. We'll include concurrency guidance in the docs we share.
12:38 Lena Park: Ok, time for a short recap. Action items: we'll send pricing and the benchmark/template, Marcus will include Optimize tuning notes, and you'll share traces. Then we schedule a pilot kickoff.
12:52 Amira Singh: Sounds good, thanks.
12:55 Jonas Meyer: Cool, appreciate the walkthrough.
12:58 Sara Lee: Thank you.
13:05 Lena Park: Thanks everyone, we'll follow up via email — expect materials by Monday.
13:12 Speaker 4: (call end)
13:20 TRANSCRIPT NOTES: occasional ASR mistakes present (product names sometimes mis-heard as "optimiser"), speaker overlaps, some muted listeners. The demo included links: Console tour deck (drive.redwood/example), benchmark template (sheets.redwood/benchmarks), security pack (redwood.com/security/pac-pack).
13:40 RECAP: Per-route visibility, cache & batching recommendations, quantization profiles, Dedicated economics, pilot path agreed. Next step: exchange traces and pricing.
